cleanIntro: Christensen's own book for the Modern Hunting Rifle. The working strip is short — magazine or floor plate, then the bolt — and the one part that is not obvious is the bolt release, which must be held fully down or the bolt will not clear the action. Two things set this rifle apart from Christensen's other bolt guns. It is a modular chassis rifle: the stock, grip and forearm are separate modules, each with its own fastener and torque figure, and the adjustable comb rides on rods that the book has you lift out and clean. And it can be built with a hinged floor plate over an internal magazine or converted to a detachable dropbox magazine, so how you empty it depends on which your rifle has. The book bans graphite lubricants outright, and the action screws go back at 65 inch-pounds, front screw first.

steps.title: Safety all the way back to S
steps.action: The safety lever sits to the right of the bolt shroud on a right-handed rifle. Move it all the way back to S before anything else. If it will not go, do not force it: the lever only reaches S on a cocked rifle, and the book warns that forcing it on an uncocked rifle can damage the trigger. An owner who meets a stiff safety is usually holding a rifle that has already been dry-fired.
steps.aside: WARNING: NEVER FORCE THE SAFETY LEVER TO THE SAFE POSITION IF THE RIFLE IS NOT COCKED. FAILURE TO DO SO MAY RESULT IN A DAMAGED TRIGGER.
steps.quote: To engage the safety, move the safety lever all the way back to the “S” position.
steps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Hunting Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed in the document — SAFETY FEATURES, printed p.4

steps.title: Detachable magazine: catch, then down
steps.action: If your rifle feeds from a detachable dropbox magazine, press the magazine catch lever and draw the magazine straight down. Do it before the bolt is worked: a magazine left in place simply feeds the next round when you open and close the bolt to check the chamber.
steps.aside: WARNING: IF THE CARTRIDGES IN THE MAGAZINE OR MAG BOX ARE NOT REMOVED PRIOR TO THIS PROCEDURE, ANY ROUNDS LEFT IN IT COULD BE CHAMBERED, WHICH COULD LEAD TO AN UNINTENTIONAL DISCHARGE. THE RIFLE IS CAPABLE OF FIRING WITH A ROUND CHAMBERED AND THE MAGAZINE REMOVED.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine by depressing the magazine catch lever and pulling the magazine down.
steps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Hunting Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed in the document — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, printed p.13

steps.title: Hinged floor plate: hold it as it springs open
steps.action: If your rifle has the internal magazine, press the magazine release lever and the floor plate springs open under the follower spring. Keep a hand under it and let it open slowly, so the cartridges come out into your palm rather than onto the floor. This empties the internal magazine without running a single round through the action.
steps.aside: Hold and slowly open the floor plate to ensure unused cartridges do not fall out unintentionally.
steps.quote: Pressing the magazine release lever, the floor plate will spring open when the release lever is pressed.
steps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Hunting Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed in the document — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, printed p.13

steps.title: Then the bolt back, chamber checked
steps.action: Now open the bolt to extract anything in the chamber, then look in and confirm the chamber is empty. The order is the book’s own — its clearing instruction is safety to SAFE, magazine out, THEN the bolt back and the chamber checked — and the book is plain that this rifle will fire with a round chambered and the magazine out.
steps.aside: IMPORTANT: Put the safety selector in the “SAFE” position. Remove the magazine, THEN pull the bolt back and check the chamber.
steps.quote: Open the bolt to extract any chambered cartridge.
steps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Hunting Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed in the document — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, printed p.13

steps.title: Unloaded, and safety glasses on
steps.action: Christensen asks for safety glasses for disassembly and maintenance, not just for shooting — there are springs under tension in the bolt and the floor plate, and solvent gets flicked about once the brushes come out.
steps.aside: WARNING: ALWAYS UNLOAD YOUR FIREARM BEFORE CLEANING, LUBRICATION, DISASSEMBLY OR REASSEMBLY.
steps.quote: WARNING: ALWAYS WEAR SAFETY GLASSES WHEN DISASSEMBLING, MAINTAINING OR ASSEMBLING YOUR FIREARM.
steps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Hunting Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed in the document — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.14

steps.title: Bolt handle up, all the way back
steps.action: Point the rifle in a safe direction, rotate the bolt handle up and draw the bolt fully rearward until it stops, and confirm once more that the rifle is not loaded. The bolt has to be at the very back of its travel for the release to let it out.
steps.quote: Rotate Bolt Handle and pull all the way back.
steps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Hunting Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed in the document — REMOVE BOLT ASSEMBLY, printed p.14

steps.title: Hold the bolt release FULLY down and slide the bolt out
steps.action: Depress the bolt release completely and keep it held while you slide the bolt out of the rifle. 'Fully' matters: a half-pressed release lets the bolt move and then stop dead, which is easy to mistake for an obstruction and start pulling against. Held right down, the bolt comes straight out.
steps.quote: While depressing Bolt Release fully, slide the Bolt from the Rifle.
steps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Hunting Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed in the document — REMOVE BOLT ASSEMBLY, printed p.14

steps.title: Look through the bore from the breech
steps.action: With the bolt out you can see down the barrel from the breech end. Check it for obstructions or debris now. A patch or a lodged bullet found here is a cleaning-rod job; if a rod and patch will not clear it, the book sends the rifle to a qualified gunsmith rather than having you force it.
steps.aside: Use a cleaning rod and patch to remove any obstructions. If they are insufficient for the job, take your rifle to a qualified gunsmith.
steps.quote: Check the barrel for any obstructions or debris by looking from the breech side.
steps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Hunting Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed in the document — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, printed p.13

steps.title: Field strip complete — the chassis only comes apart if you must
steps.action: Bolt and magazine out is the working strip, and it is all the routine clean needs. Christensen does publish lifting the barrelled action out of the chassis, and Deep Clean covers it together with the comb-bar clean, but the action screws go back at a stated torque, so do not take the chassis apart casually.
steps.quote: Remove the barreled action from the chassis
steps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Hunting Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed in the document — REMOVING BARRELED ACTION, printed p.14

deepSteps.title: Barrelled action out — only with a torque wrench to hand
deepSteps.action: With the bolt out and the rifle confirmed empty, remove the two action screws from the underside and lift the barrelled action free of the chassis. If it sticks, the book's remedy is a nylon-headed hammer tapping the top of the mounting lug — not prying at the stock. Do not start this unless you can put the screws back at 65 inch-pounds.
deepSteps.aside: NOTE: If the barreled action does not remove easily, use a nylon head or similar hammer to tap the top of mounting lug to begin loosening the barreled action from the chassis/stock assembly.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the two action screws on the underside of the rifle and lift the barreled action free from the chassis.
deepSteps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Hunting Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed in the document — REPLACING FOREARM, printed p.20

deepSteps.title: Comb bar: screw out, button down, comb up
deepSteps.action: With the rifle unloaded and the bolt out, take out the comb retaining screw through the flush-cup mount, then hold the comb adjust button down and lift the adjustable comb fully out of the stock. The comb rides on rods, and grit on those rods is what makes the comb bind or refuse to lock at height.
deepSteps.aside: Depress comb adjust button and lift the adjustable comb fully from the stock.
deepSteps.quote: Remove comb retaining screw through the flush cup mount.
deepSteps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Hunting Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed in the document — CLEANING COMB HEIGHT ADJUSTMENT BAR, printed p.15

deepSteps.title: Clean the rods, then back in at 3 inch-pounds
deepSteps.action: Clean the rods and the comb mechanism, then reassemble with a low-strength removable thread locker on the retaining screw and torque it to just 3 inch-pounds. That is a very small figure — a screw run down by feel here will be far too tight.
deepSteps.aside: Clean the rods and comb mechanism.
deepSteps.quote: Reassemble using low strength removable thread locker and torque to 3 in. lbs.
deepSteps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Hunting Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed in the document — CLEANING COMB HEIGHT ADJUSTMENT BAR, printed p.15

deepSteps.title: Chamber and locking lugs — push and twist
deepSteps.action: Put a chamber brush on the rod, apply solvent, and work it into the chamber and the locking-lug recesses by pushing and twisting rather than stroking. Then swap to a swab holder and run a solvent swab through the chamber and out the muzzle brake. On heavy carbon let the solvent sit before wiping; the book allows a nylon bore brush, used with care.
deepSteps.aside: To remove carbon build up, let the solvent sit then wipe clean. A nylon bore brush may be used with care to remove heavy carbon buildup.
deepSteps.quote: Install the chamber brush on the cleaning rod, apply cleaning solvent and insert into the chamber and locking lugs.
deepSteps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Hunting Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed in the document — RIFLE MAINTENANCE, printed p.16

deepSteps.title: Bore from the breech, and never reverse the brush
deepSteps.action: Every patch and brush goes in from the breech end and out the muzzle. Once a bore brush is in the bore it goes all the way through before it comes back — the book prints that caution three times, because dragging bristles backwards over the rifling tears them out and lodges them.
deepSteps.aside: CAUTION: DO NOT REVERSE THE DIRECTION OF THE BORE BRUSH WHILE IT IS IN THE BORE.
deepSteps.quote: ALWAYS push the cleaning/oiling patch from the breech end.
deepSteps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Hunting Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed in the document — CLEANING, printed p.15

deepSteps.title: Solvents — anything but graphite
deepSteps.action: Use a good solvent for metal fouling and lubricate generously, but obey the book's one absolute ban: no lubricant containing graphite, under any condition, because it encourages rapid corrosion in this rifle. Read the label of any dry-film or moly product before it goes near the action.
deepSteps.quote: Under NO condition should any lubricant containing graphite be used with your rifle. Graphite can encourage rapid corrosion in your rifle.
deepSteps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Hunting Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed in the document — CLEANING SOLVENTS AND LUBRICANTS, printed p.15

deepSteps.title: Light oil on bore, chamber, barrel and lugs
deepSteps.action: Lightly lubricate the bore, the chamber and the outside of the barrel, run a lubricated swab from the receiver to the muzzle brake, and oil the locking lugs. Light is the word: the book warns that preservative in the bore raises pressure on firing, so whatever goes in comes back out with a dry patch before the rifle is shot.
deepSteps.quote: Lightly lubricate the bore, chamber and outer surface of the barrel.
deepSteps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Hunting Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed in the document — RIFLE MAINTENANCE, printed p.16

deepSteps.title: Keep each bolt with its own rifle, and wash your hands
deepSteps.action: If you own more than one rifle, keep each bolt with its own action — the book capitalises this, and a bolt in the wrong rifle is a headspace question, not a housekeeping one. And the fouling you have just brushed out contains lead; wash before you eat or smoke.
deepSteps.aside: WARNING: LEAD MAY BE PRESENT IN THE FOULING OF A DIRTY RIFLE. AVOID CONTACT WITH IT AND CLEAN HANDS AFTERWARD TO AVOID INGESTING LEAD.
deepSteps.quote: WARNING! DO NOT INTERCHANGE BOLTS BETWEEN RIFLES.
deepSteps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Hunting Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed in the document — RIFLE MAINTENANCE, printed p.16

deepSteps.title: Back together: thread locker, 65 inch-pounds, front screw first
deepSteps.action: Reassemble in reverse order, putting thread-locking compound back on every screw. The action screws go to 65 inch-pounds, front screw first, with the recoil lug slid forward against the chassis as you tighten. Then the bolt: of its two front lugs one is grooved and one is not, and the grooves line up with the grooves in the action.
deepSteps.aside: REAPPLY THREAD-LOCKING COMPOUND TO ALL SCREWS
deepSteps.quote: Follow disassembly instructions in reverse order.
deepSteps.cite: Christensen Arms Modern Hunting Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed in the document — REASSEMBLY, printed p.16

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Bolt and magazine out; rifle on its side with the ejection port up, or upright in a gun vise
Correct-calibre brush on the rod with solvent, pushed through from the BREECH end to the muzzle several times
Never reverse the brush while it is in the bore
Patches on the tip, a clean one each time, until a patch comes out clean
One oil-saturated patch through, then a clean dry patch to take the excess back out

cleaning.name: CHAMBER & LUGS
tasks: Chamber brush with solvent, pushed and twisted into the chamber and locking lugs
Solvent swab through the chamber and out the muzzle brake
Let solvent sit on heavy carbon, then wipe clean
Light lubricant on the locking lugs

cleaning.name: BOLT & ACTION
tasks: Wipe the bolt down and inspect it
Lubricate the moving parts generously — no graphite, ever
Never fit another rifle's bolt to this action

cleaning.name: COMB, STOCK & MUZZLE BRAKE
tasks: If the comb binds: lift it out and clean the rods and comb mechanism
Stock wiped with a damp rag, warm water or mild household cleaner
Barrel wiped with gun oil and dried back to restore the finish
Clean the baffles in the muzzle brake while cleaning the rifle
Inspect barrel and stock for cracks, bends or breaks

reassembly: Reassemble in the reverse order of disassembly.
Reapply thread-locking compound to all screws.
Action screws to 65 inch-pounds: recoil lug slid forward against the chassis, front screw first, then the rear.
Comb retaining screw with low-strength removable thread locker, 3 inch-pounds.
Insert the bolt with the grooved lug matched to the grooves in the action.
Clean and dry the bore before the rifle is fired.
fncheck: Christensen's book for this rifle says a functional check should follow any disassembly and reassembly, with the rifle unloaded and the magazine removed, but it prints no functional-check procedure of its own. What the book does state: the safety lever goes all the way back to S only on a cocked rifle and must never be forced there; the trigger is adjusted at the factory and every adjustment to it must be done at the factory; and in case of a malfunction you stop and contact Christensen Arms if the manual does not resolve it.
